extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of public administration and governance (including policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and evaluating administrative systems and the proper relations between political organs and administrative (executive, quasi‑judicial, and technical) officials. Covers limits of political control, tenure, independence, and system forms (hierarchical discretion vs law‑bound administration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordination of executive function to politics
rubrics_metrics.description: "This executive function must therefore of necessity be subordinated to the function of politics.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive authorities (those charged with general execution of law) should be subject to the control of the political body ultimately entrusted with expressing the state will, so that lawmaking and law‑execution remain coordinated and the government remains responsive to popular control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political control is ineffective for quasi‑judicial duties
rubrics_metrics.description: "No control of a political character can bring about that administrative officers will discharge better their quasi‑judicial duties...","
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political oversight cannot meaningfully improve discretionary, quasi‑judicial decisions; such oversight risks undermining impartiality without improving substantive judgment. Courts treat many quasi‑judicial administrative functions akin to judicial functions and protect them from partisan control (examples: Wilson v. The Mayor; Pike v. Megoun).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political control cannot improve fact‑gathering or technical investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: "No control which a political body can have over a body intrusted with the acquisition of facts and the gathering of information can result in the gathering of more facts or the acquisition of more exact information.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that is statistical, semi‑scientific, or investigatory is degraded by political involvement because it biases investigators and pollutes sources of truth. Such tasks require professional independence to preserve accuracy and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit political oversight to general conduct, not concrete discretionary acts
rubrics_metrics.description: "All that the legislature, or any political body, can do is to see to it... that persons discharging these administrative functions are efficient and impartial. Their general conduct, but not their concrete actions, should be subject to control.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political bodies should aim to ensure administrative integrity, efficiency, and impartiality via general oversight, standards, and appointments, but avoid micromanaging discretionary decisions (except to check gross abuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extending political control beyond ensuring administrative integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "any attempt to exercise such a control beyond the attempt to insure administrative integrity is likely to produce evil rather than good.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overreach of political control into technical, investigatory, or quasi‑judicial domains produces bias, corruption, and inefficiency; the warning is illustrated by harms to election administration, tax administration, and truth‑finding functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an administrative force free from political influence for semi‑scientific/quasi‑judicial/technical work
rubrics_metrics.description: "For the most advantageous discharge of this branch of the function of administration there should be organized a force of governmental agents absolutely free from the influence of politics.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize and staff semi‑scientific, quasi‑judicial, and technical branches as career, nonpartisan services with protections against partisan interference to secure foresight, discretion, truthful inquiry, and impartial treatment of individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative officers performing impartial technical work should have judicial‑like status
rubrics_metrics.description: "The position of such officers should be much the same as is that which has been by universal consent assigned to judges.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because their work is apolitical and requires impartiality and expertise, these officers should enjoy institutional protections (status, independence) analogous to judicial officers to insulate them from partisan pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasonable permanence of tenure for semi‑scientific, quasi‑judicial, and technical positions
rubrics_metrics.description: "They should have permanence of tenure because the excellence of their work is often conditioned by the fact that they are expert, and expertness comes largely from long practice. Reasonable permanence of tenure is absolutely necessary...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer tenure supports accumulation of expertise and administrative efficiency for technical and ministerial staff (clerical/ministerial officers as well), reducing costs and improving performance. Permanence may be secured by law or public opinion (examples: Germany, England).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid permanence of tenure for high‑level executive officers with broad discretionary powers
rubrics_metrics.description: "Care should be taken, however, that permanence of tenure be not given to those distinctly executive officers to whom is entrusted the general execution of the law.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long tenure for top executive officials risks detaching the government from popular control and enabling an entrenched administrative machine that can undermine representative government. Political control mechanisms (removal, short terms) are appropriate for these roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipal administration needs greater insulation from politics
rubrics_metrics.description: "The necessity for this separation of politics from administration is very marked in the case of municipal government... the influence of politics on municipal government is worse than on state administration.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because municipal government is predominantly administrative and local politics can be entangled with state and national politics, municipalities especially benefit from distinguishing administrative functions from partisan control to prevent partiality, inefficiency, and sacrifice of local interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize dual limits: political control over execution, and apolitical administrative domains
rubrics_metrics.description: "Safety lies alone in frankly recognizing both that there should be a control over the general execution of the law and that there is a part of the work of administration into which politics should not enter.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy design must simultaneously ensure popular oversight of law execution (to reflect the state will) while carving out protected spheres (technical, quasi‑judicial, investigatory) where political interference is excluded to maintain efficiency and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design administrative systems with appropriate level of discretion vs legal direction
rubrics_metrics.description: "The administrative systems of the world belong in a greater or less degree to one of two main forms... officers... are vested with large discretion... or they are vested with almost no discretion at all... being merely the instruments of state organs which determine not only what shall be done, but also how...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose between hierarchical, discretionary administrations and law‑bound, minimal‑discretion administrations based on tradeoffs: discretion supports administrative initiative and detail management; strict legal direction curbs despotism and promotes obedience to law but may require detailed legislation and judicial enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where administration is decentralized and judicial control is primary, legislate detailed duties and use short terms/elections for executive officers
rubrics_metrics.description: "The judicial control by which it is accompanied is not suited to secure anything except obedience to the law... These questions of expediency must be determined by the legislature, which must descend in its legislation into the greatest details... Such executive officers are therefore given short terms...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a decentralized system emphasizing rule of law over hierarchical supervision, the legislature must provide detailed statutory duties and rely on courts for enforcement; to preserve popular control, give executive officers short terms and frequent elections, recognizing limits of judicial oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance permanence of tenure and party strength to avoid perversion of the popular will
rubrics_metrics.description: "Too great strength in the administrative organization tends to make popular government impossible... On the other hand... permanence of tenure in the lower grades... can also be made use of, where there is a strong party organization, to nullify the popular will.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers must avoid extremes: excessive administrative permanence with weak parties can subvert elections via administrative power; excessive politicization can subvert administration. Design tenure, appointment, and removal rules to preserve both efficiency and democratic responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish ministerial acts from discretionary acts and limit court and legislative intervention accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: "The courts... have voluntarily confined their jurisdiction to ministerial acts, and have refused to exercise a control over discretionary acts... The only possible exception...is... that discretion is not grossly abused.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify administrative functions: ministerial acts (subject to judicial enforcement) should be controlled to ensure obedience to law; discretionary acts should generally be left to professional judgment, with judicial remedy reserved for gross abuses, recognizing practical limits of both legislative and judicial oversight.
